violations: Sora is specified for the rupee prices in the hook menu, in the S07 'Masala Dosa ₹80' / 'Ghee Roast Dosa ₹110' kinetic lines and in the S08 ₹150 number flight. Sora-Variable.ttf has no U+20B9 glyph (I checked its cmap), so ₹ would render in a fallback font. Set prices in Plus Jakarta Sans or Space Mono.
The 4.5 s hook packs in the outline draw-on, five dish lines, the logo tile, 'SETU Food' and two captions. That breaks one-idea-at-a-time, and the owner's opening line has to compete with the menu.
S06 chips: there are taps at 48.70, 48.95 and 49.20, but nothing changes until a single crossfade at 49.25, so action and result are out of sync.
S04 opens with a 'back' push from signed-in Home to the sign-in screen. That reads as in-app navigation that does not exist; a chapter wipe would be more honest.
S07 coffee: one ADD tap cuts straight to the '2' state. The caption says 'Tap plus', but + only gets a ring.

The narration reads like a manual: eight 'Tap …' instructions. Captions are on screen almost continuously (95.6 s at 2.45 words/s on average) with little breathing room, and no line welcomes faculty or staff.
'Adjust the pin' is captioned, but no pin move is shown; the map only gets 'Use this location'.
bestIdeas: Story-style 8-segment progress rail with numbered chapters. Gen Z already knows this pattern, and it also shows faculty where they are.
The 'View cart' pill grows (#0033DA mask) into the real cart screen: a clean action-to-result cut.
The cart's ₹150 lifts, arcs and docks onto the Confirm order amount card.
A TIME-LAPSE tag over the status run is honest about the roughly 20-minute wait and avoids implying delivery speed.
A cropped inset of the app's own location explainer, labelled OPTIONAL, while the phone stays on step 2. It shows that GPS is optional without a detour.
The map push to 1.8x, focused at y 575, keeps the app's 'SETU delivers…' subtitle out of frame while the Google attribution stays visible.
The QR second phone starts on 'Waiting for the stall to accept your order', so the accept-first order is visible.
The end-card disclaimer is held 7.7 s, comfortable for 29 words.
Light trails from the email digits to the code boxes, synced to the 7-frame typing sequence.

violations: The cart-math numerals (Sora 800 96 px) and the ₹150 number flight (Sora 800) include ₹, which Sora does not have, so a fallback glyph would render.

Several objects fly into the phone at once: three cuisine chips into the tabs (57.3–57.9) and two order-line chips into the cart (68.6–69.0). The project STYLE.md forbids this, and both scene seams get busy.

The left column collides: the motion-graphic stepper at (140,260) overlaps the cuisine chips parked at y 250 in s06, and the docked 'Home · B-212' chip at y 860 touches the top of a two-line caption plate.
Cause comes after effect: Home is tapped at 45.7 on 14-type-room/f0000, where it is already selected, and '+' is tapped at 66.35 after 05-coffee-two has shown 2 since 66.2.
End card: the 29-word disclaimer is fully legible for only 4.7 s. That meets the 4 s minimum with little margin, and 'Dinner, sorted.' overlaps the tagline's entrance.
About 23 minutes of real order time (7:02 to 7:25 pm) are compressed into roughly 11 s with no TIME-LAPSE label.
No real UI appears until 6.5 s, and the phone only at 15.1 s. The hook also recreates the Food / Commute SOON / Utilities SOON pills as motion graphics outside the phone, which is borderline fake UI.
The map push at 1.35x leaves the app's 'SETU delivers inside…' sheet subtitle in frame. It is not featured, but it could be framed out. 'Fine-tune the pin' is captioned, but no pin move is shown.
bestIdeas: A web-to-phone match cut on the shared 'SIGNING IN AS Customer' form; the desktop form at 0.81x equals the phone screen width.
The pin unfolds into a 'Home · B-212' address card, docks as a chip, and later lands in the real Home header. This carries one action across three scenes.
The picked cuisine chips park in the left column, then land on the real Home tabs (preference, then result).

One persona (Aarav, Nehru Hall, dinner time) plus one explicit line, 'students, faculty, staff'. It feels warm for Gen Z and includes faculty; 'Tonight: dosa.' and 'Dinner, sorted.' are light without being hype.
The quote 'You will see a status timeline, not a rider on a map.' sits beside the status rail, and the rail dissolves into the real progress card.
A 'Live on Home' beat using the real live order card (05-home-live-card).
'Something off? Report it from the order.' with 'Food quality or hygiene' quoted, a trust beat that faculty will value.
A campus outline with the real nehruHall data point bookends the hook, the zone check and the end card.
It avoids the review placeholder 'Hot, on time…' (a delivery-time risk) and skips 11-review-note.
An editorial hairline 'or' wipe from the permission explainer to search, and a band wipe for the new-customer chapter instead of a fake in-app back.
It is built on the real kit.js helpers, so it is the easiest to build in the existing HyperFrames setup.

violations: Four 'PROVEN · …' stamps. The word is close to hype and overclaims: a label or a cart total cannot 'prove' approval or no commission. Faculty will read it as spin, and it undercuts the honest tone.

'DEMO ENVIRONMENT · SAMPLE STALLS' stays on screen continuously from 15.0 to 105.2 s. The brief asks to say it once. A permanent DEMO tag clutters every frame and blurs the moment where the OTP DEMO label drops.
The slowest start: 16.8 s pass before the walkthrough begins. The runtime is 113.8 s, inside the range but off the 112 s target.

S05 is overloaded: the GPS route, the search route and the map all fit in 13.6 s, with holds of 0.5–0.7 s on the GPS reading, the picker, the results and the return to confirm. Showing a GPS fix and then searching anyway muddles the 'optional' message.
The frame gets busy: chapter label, 4-dot indicator, demo note, callouts, stamps and kinetic type are often on screen together.
The hook shows the post-onboarding Home with sample stalls before any demo disclosure. The grey initial tiles make a weak food hook.
It rings the step-1 line 'Stakeholders see your first name…', which is not in the verified facts.
bestIdeas: Local state changes play as circular reveals centred on the tap (ADD to stepper, chips, toggle, stars), never as a full-screen crossfade.
A focus mask keeps fact 3's licence text and the 'Recorded against your account…' sub-line dark. Compliance is built into the design.
Promise chips are lifted straight off the real web stats into a persistent 4-dot indicator. Keep this system and drop 'PROVEN', for example by using a plain check.
A type rule that sets ₹ in Plus Jakarta Sans because Sora lacks the glyph; I confirmed this against the font file.
Dish lines turn into order lines and fly into the 'View cart' pill, which then morphs into the cart.
A blue fill from 'Start ordering' and a circular wipe from 'Place order · ₹150' are consistent action-to-result transitions.
Correct cause and effect: go back to 13-confirm-search and tap Home before cutting to 14-type-room/f0000; for coffee, ADD, then +, then reveal 2.
A silent end card gives the disclaimer 6 s of clean reading, and the fine print adds 'Demo QR is not a real payment code'.
Grain seeded by frame number keeps the seekable render deterministic.
The real Home scroll clip is on the phone by 2.2 s.

rationale:
From a motion and audience angle, B-story is the strongest film.

B has the most cinematic connections that are still motivated, and each one ties an action to its result: the web-to-phone match cut, the pin becoming the address card and then the Home header, the cuisine chips landing on the Home tabs, the dish chips becoming cart lines, the ₹150 flight, and the campus/Nehru Hall motif opening and closing the film. It also has the best tone. One warm student story plus an explicit 'students, faculty, staff' line gives Gen Z energy without shutting out faculty, and a 'Report it' beat builds trust.

I checked B against the final captures and found no errors: prep time 7:24 pm, timeline 7:02 to 7:25 pm, separate demo order IDs (VGKQ for QR, BCQK for cash), every mark coordinate, and the nehruHall point. It meets every hard rule.

A-tutorial is the safest and clearest, and is close to B on compliance (50 vs 52). Its coordinates and copy are exact, it has a TIME-LAPSE tag and a 7.7 s disclaimer. But it plays like a manual (eight 'Tap …' lines), its hook is overloaded, and a few taps are out of sync with their results.

C-value has the most rigorous motion principles (circular local reveals, a focus mask, the ₹ font rule). Its four 'PROVEN' stamps and a demo tag held for 90 s hurt tone and compliance, and it starts slowly (16.8 s before the walkthrough begins, 113.8 s total).

Before building B, apply these fixes and additions:
1. Set every ₹ in Plus Jakarta Sans or Space Mono. Sora-Variable.ttf has no ₹ glyph, which affects B's cart math and number flight and A's prices; C already handles this.
2. Stagger the chip flights instead of flying several objects into the phone at once, and fix the clash between the left-column stepper and the parked chips.
3. Take C's tap order: return to 13-confirm-search and tap Home before cutting to f0000, and tap coffee ADD, then +, then reveal 2.
4. Add A's TIME-LAPSE tag over the status run.
5. Start the end card about 1.5 s earlier so the disclaimer is readable for at least 6 s.
6. Frame the map like A (1.8x at y 575) so 'SETU delivers…' is off screen.
7. Optionally add C's circular reveals and focus mask.
